channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Federal Reserve: September hike bias shifts – ING
item.description: ING’s James Knightley argues Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech has shifted the Federal Reserve’s reaction function toward a September rate hike, even though ING’s macro projections suggest the Fed could wait.

item.title: Economists agree: ECB to hike rates on September 10 – Reuters poll
item.description: According to the latest Reuters poll, the 65 economists surveyed have favored that the European Central Bank (ECB) will raise the deposit rate by 25 basis points (bps) to 2.50%.

item.title: WTI Oil hits highs near $91 as risks of an all-out war in the Middle East grow
item.description: Crude prices resumed their upside trend on Thursday after some hesitation on Wednesday, with the US benchmark West Texas Intermediate reaching session highs a few cents below $91.00 per barrel, almost 10% up on the week so far.

item.title: US Dollar: Near-term stabilization view – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes the US Dollar (USD) is softer mainly against the Japanese Yen and Swiss Franc, with Brent Oil nearing $100.

item.title: Gold climbs as Yen-led US Dollar decline outweighs hawkish Fed expectations
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends its rebound on Thursday after slipping below $4,300 to a nearly four-week low on the previous day. A sharp rally in the Japanese Yen (JPY) weighs on the US Dollar (USD), helping the precious metal regain ground.

item.title: Indian Rupee rallies on strong foreign inflows through FCNR deposits
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades strongly against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday, extending the rally to near 94.28.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar gains against US Dollar due to unfavorable US NFP backdrop
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) is up 0.16% at around 0.5860 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Thursday.

item.title: Euro tumbles as Japanese Yen surges on intervention threats
item.description: EUR/JPY falls sharply on Thursday and trades around 181.40 at the time of writing, down 1.37% on the day. The Japanese Yen (JPY) strengthens significantly against the Euro (EUR), supported by renewed warnings from Japanese authorities over foreign exchange market moves.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD recovery, likely to be challenged around $4,470
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) is trading higher on Thursday, returning to levels above $4.400 after bouncing from three-week lows near $4,280 on Wednesday.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Swiss data supports dip-buying case – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists note Swiss August Consumer Price Index (CPI) and second-quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP) surprised to the upside, triggering profit-taking in EUR/CHF and USD/CHF but leaving Swiss National Bank (SNB) policy expectations unchanged.

item.title: 0.8600 under pressure: EUR/GBP at two-month highs following Services PMIs
item.description: The Euro (EUR) extends gains against a weaker British Pound (GBP) for the fourth consecutive day on Thursday, following downward revisions of both the Eurozone and UK Services Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) figures.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: BoC inflation focus and valuation divergence – MUFG
item.description: Derek Halpenny at MUFG notes the Canadian Dollar’s (CAD) immediate advance after the Bank of Canada left rates unchanged at 2.25% but signalled greater concern over inflation.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Thursday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $65.88 per troy ounce, up 0.87% from the $65.31 it cost on Wednesday.

item.title: Japan’s Mimura keeps threat of FX intervention alive
item.description: Japan’s top currency diplomat Atsushi Mimura reiterates on Thursday that authorities remain ready to act in the foreign exchange market, as Tokyo continues to closely monitor currency moves.

item.title: Polish Zloty: NBP language turns cautious after FX pressure – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose notes that NBP Governor Adam Glapinski used G20 remarks to shift towards a more neutral, flexible stance, avoiding earlier dovish hints of imminent rate cuts. With August CPI surprising hawkishly and the Zloty underperforming CE3 peers, the bank is seen on the back foot.

item.title: Japanese Yen strengthens following hawkish BoJ comments
item.description: USD/JPY extends its losses for the second consecutive day, trading around 156.80 during the European hours on Thursday.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Pullback eases with upside focus on 0.7200 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report AUD/USD dipped to 0.7122 before a strong rebound to 0.7176, leaving intraday price action in a 0.7140–0.7180 range. Downward momentum is fading and a break above 0.7190 would confirm 0.7120 is out of reach.

item.title: ISM Services PMI Preview: US service sector expected to expand in August
item.description: On Thursday, we’ll get the latest read on the US service sector when the Institute for Supply Management (ISM) publishes its August gauge. Consensus points to a marginal improvement to 54.3 from July’s 54.1.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention jitters linger – ING
item.description: Chris Turner at ING notes that a near 1% drop in USD/JPY within minutes, followed by another slide, sparked talk of renewed Japanese intervention after the Bank of Japan’s earlier $96 billion sales.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD struggles to extend upside above $66.25, NFP data awaited
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) struggles to extend Wednesday’s strong recovery move above $66.25 during the European trading session on Thursday. The white metal could remain sideways as investors await the United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data for August, which will be released on Friday.

item.title: Dow Jones futures gain as oil prices, US yields ease
item.description: Dow Jones futures gain by 0.18% to trade near 53,220 during European hours on Thursday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures advance by 0.16% to trade near 7,690, while Nasdaq 100 futures inch higher by 0.03% to trade around 29,200.

item.title: US Dollar: Hedging impulse fades as holdings stabilize – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes that the July FOMC-driven Dollar hedging impulse has largely run its course, with early signs of USD buying returning against EUR, MXN and CAD.

item.title: Forex Today: Japanese Yen extends rally, markets await US data
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Thursday, September 3:

item.title: Euro remains flat above 1.1600 after softer-than-expected Eurozone services activity
item.description: The Euro (EUR) picks up against a somewhat softer US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday, but upside attempts are frail, after last week's 0.8% decline and Eurozone PMI data have failed to boost confidence in the Eurozone's economic outlook.

item.title: Oil: Rally pace moderates after Iran strikes – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank analysts note that Brent extended its rally and closed above USD95, although gains moderated after President Trump suggested the renewed US bombing campaign against Iran could be short-lived.

item.title: Gold stands firm as USD dives to one-week low; Fed hike bets cap gains
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) built on its recovery from a nearly four-week low for the second straight day on Thursday, though it remains below $4,450 through the first half of the European session. The US Dollar (USD) plummets to a one-week low and is seen as a key factor supporting the commodity.

item.title: British Pound gains capped as fiscal, geopolitical risks persist
item.description: GBP/USD gains after two days of losses, trading around 1.3500 during the European hours on Thursday. The currency pair experiences an upward push as a sharp rally in the Japanese Yen (JPY) weighed heavily on the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: BoJ mulls hiking interest rates to 1.25% in September meeting – Bloomberg
item.description: According to a report from Bloomberg, the Bank of Japan (BoJ) is leaning toward raising its benchmark interest rate by a quarter point in the two-day meeting ending on September 18 in response to upward price risks.

item.title: British Pound: Downside seen limited near 1.3465 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note GBP/USD extended its decline to 1.3475 before rebounding, closing at 1.3485. Intraday bias remains lower, but any weakness is seen limited to a test of 1.3465, with 1.3510 marking a shift back to range trading.

item.title: WTI remains broadly firm around $90 as oil shipments through Hormuz remain restricted
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), futures on NYMEX, consolidates in a tight range around $88.85 during the European trading session on Thursday.
